contexts.text: The idea of the rejection of evil... is attended with a certain swiftness.
Saul and Jonathan... were swifter than eagles ()... Swiftness, in the Word, when predicated of intelligence, = the affection of truth.
His horses are swifter than eagles () = reasoning against truths, and destroying them; for by swift, and haste, in the Word, is signified being stirred by affection and desire.

Ye said... We will ride upon the swift; therefore shall they that pursue you be made swift ()... To ride upon the swift = to covet and love those things which are of one's own understanding and the derivative thought and reasoning. That falsities will then break in and take possession, is signified by... therefore shall they that pursue you be made swift. Swift, and haste = that which is done from cupidity or from love.

The tongue of the stammerers shall be swift to speak () = ... that those who are hardly able to apprehend the truths of the Church will acknowledge them from affection. Swift is predicated of affection.
